newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities steady to higher.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended steady to slightly higher in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Monday.

"The interbank rate rose slightly today but there was little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were quietly steady but bond prices were slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months was unchanged from last Friday's yield of 1.45/1.40 percent and one-year unchanged at 1.70/1.65 percent.

Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$99.20/99.30 compared with last Friday's close of S$99.15/99.25, September 2001 at S$98.82/96.87 against S$96.79/96.89 and June 2003 at S$94.82/94.87 from S$94.79/94.89.
The interbank rate rose to 3-7/16 3-5/16 percent versus last Friday's 3-3/8 3-1/4 percent.
